vārayituṃ.meaning_2: to prevent; to restrain; to ward off; to turn away
vārayituṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Infinitive of the causative vārayati. In the text it depends on arahāmi and ussahe; the object is kumāraṃ or no.

etadakkhā.meaning_2: this saw; saw this; told this
etadakkhā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of etaṃ (pron) + akkhā (aorist of akkhāti, 'told'). The text has etadakkhā; the commentary glosses as 'told this'. Third person singular aorist.
etadakkhā.example_2: na cāpi me koci naṃ etadakkhā;

iṇadānaṃ.meaning_2: debt payment; repayment of debt; lending money (at interest)
iṇadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of iṇa (debt) and dāna (giving, payment). Nominative and accusative singular in the verse; it heads a list of livelihoods together with kasivāṇijjā.

carātu.meaning_2: let him walk; let him go; let him practice
carātu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Imperative 3rd singular of carati, used three times in the verse with the sense 'let it go' or 'let him roam'. The form is carātu, with the imperative ending -tu.

māsasānā.meaning_2: hoping for fruit in a month; looking forward to fruit after a month
māsasānā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of māsasānā (Sinhalese and PTS editions) for māsiṃ samānā (Burmese edition); a compound of māsa (month) + sāna (from √san, seeking), nominative plural agreeing with the sowers. The text's reading is māsasānā, so the lemma may also be taken as māsasāna.
māsasānā.example_1: 4. Thale ca ninne ca vapanti bījaṃ, anūpakhette phalamāsamānā [māsasānā (sī. pī.), māsiṃ samānā (syā.)];
māsasānā.translation_1: They sow seeds on high ground and in hollows, hoping for fruit in the marshy fields.

māsiṃ.meaning_2: monthly; every month; for a month
māsiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the verse, māsiṃ appears in the phrase anūpakhette phalamāsamānā, where it may mean 'monthly' or 'for a month'. The text is uncertain, and the variant māsiṃ samānā may reflect a different parsing. The reading is not fully settled.
māsiṃ.example_1: 4. Thale ca ninne ca vapanti bījaṃ, anūpakhette phalamāsamānā [māsasānā (sī. pī.), māsiṃ samānā (syā.)];
māsiṃ.translation_1: They sow seeds on high ground and in hollows, hoping for fruit in the marshy fields.

upajotiyo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A proper name in the Jātaka verse, probably one of four gatekeepers (with Upajjhāya and Gandakucchi). Nominative singular upajotiyo in the text.
upajotiyo.example_2: 8. Kvettha gatā [kvattha gatā (syā.), kattheva bhaṭṭhā (pī.)] upajotiyo ca, upajjhāyo ca athavā gaṇḍakucchi [aṇḍakucchi (sī. syā. pī.)];
upajotiyo.translation_2: Where have those gatekeepers, Upajotiya, Upajjhaya, and Gandhakucchi gone?

aṇḍakucchi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A proper name in the text, variant reading of gaṇḍakucchi; nominative singular in the verse.
aṇḍakucchi.example_1: 8. Kvettha gatā [kvattha gatā (syā.), kattheva bhaṭṭhā (pī.)] upajotiyo ca, upajjhāyo ca athavā gaṇḍakucchi [aṇḍakucchi (sī. syā. pī.)];
aṇḍakucchi.translation_1: Where have those gatekeepers, Upajotiya, Upajjhaya, and Gandhakucchi gone?

mahakkasāvesu.meaning_2: with great impurity; greatly stained (with defilements); deeply depraved
mahakkasāvesu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Bahubbīhi compound: mahant + kasāva, 'having great stains (of defilements)'. Locative plural in the text. The PEU entry is confused.
mahakkasāvesu.translation_2: you give gifts to those who are of great impurity, to those who are evildoers and intemperate.

paṭigāya.meaning_2: sings back; recites in response; receives by singing
paṭigāya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Imperative 2nd singular in the text (paṭigāhi is a variant reading). The prefix paṭi here means 'back, in return'.
paṭigāya.example_1: ‘‘ Gantvāna rañño paṭigāhi [paṭigāyi (syā. ka.), paṭigāya (?)] gāthaṃ, api te varaṃ attamano dadeyya ’’[api nu te varaṃ attamano dadeyya (syā.), api nu te attamano varaṃ dade (ka.)].
paṭigāya.translation_1: “Go and receive the verse from the king, and he might give you a reward, being pleased.”

paṭisaṃyamissaṃ.meaning_2: restrains oneself; controls oneself; guards oneself
paṭisaṃyamissaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Future first person singular in the text (paṭisaṃyamissaṃ = paṭisaṃyamissati). The PEU splits it as pati + saṃ + yamu + ssaṃ, future of paṭisaṃyamati.
paṭisaṃyamissaṃ.example_2: Attānameva paṭisaṃyamissaṃ, na patthaye putta [puttaṃ (sī. pī.)] pasuṃ dhanaṃ vā.
paṭisaṃyamissaṃ.translation_2: I will restrain myself; I do not desire sons, cattle, or wealth.

byasanno.meaning_2: sinking; sinking down; sunk; despairing; despondent
byasanno.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Past participle of visīdati (via sandhi vi + asanna). In the verses it describes one sunk or stuck in mud and in the mire of sensual desire. Nominative singular.

mupeti.grammar: pr, 3rd sing of upeti; variant reading for upehi
mupeti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading (pī. ka.) for upehi in the second verse; the prefix upa- has assimilated to mu-. The first verse also has an uncertain mupeti. Probably an unusual spelling of upeti; the stem follows the eti pattern.
mupeti.example_2: Datvā ca bhutvā ca yathānubhāvaṃ, anindito saggamupehi [mupeti (pī. ka.)] ṭhānaṃ.
mupeti.translation_2: And having given and partaken according to your power, go to heaven, blameless.

manasī.meaning_2: in mind; mentally; (with karoti) to keep in mind; to pay attention to
manasī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Used in the phrase manasī karohi 'keep in mind; pay attention'. Possibly an absolutive-like or adverbial form of manas (locative manasi with lengthened final vowel for the metre); treated here as an indeclinable.
manasī.example_2: Imameva gāthaṃ manasī karohi, bhāsesi [bhāsehi (syā. pī. ka.)] cenaṃ parisāya majjhe.
manasī.translation_2: Keep this very verse in mind, and speak it in the midst of the assembly:

vajantyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Feminine present participle in instrumental singular, agreeing with a female animal in the verse; the form is vajantyā.
vajantyā.translation_2: A person who slept in the open, nursed while walking, and surrounded by dogs,

māgatosi.meaning_2: you have not come here; haven't you come here
māgatosi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of na + āgato + asi (na + āgata > māgata; āgata (pp of āgacchati) + asi (pr of √as)). Negative interrogative in the verse; 'māgato' is also a common word (the Magadha people), but that does not fit here. Respelled in the text as māgatosi.
māgatosi.example_2: 53. Kenānusiṭṭho idha māgatosi, vanibbaka [vaṇibbaka (sī.)] cakkhupathāni yācituṃ;
māgatosi.translation_2: By whom were you instructed, mendicant, to come here to ask for the path of the eyes?

cakkhupathāni.meaning_2: path of the eye; range of vision; something worth seeing; a sight for the eyes
cakkhupathāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Plural accusative cakkhupathāni here in the sense of things worthy to be seen, i.e. eyes. Part of a compound: cakkhupathāni yācituṃ.

māgatosmi.meaning_2: I am like a beast; I am a wild animal
māgatosmi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of māga (beast) + to (like, as) + asmi (I am). Occurs in a Jātaka verse; the exact segmentation is uncertain, possibly māga + to + asmi or māga + ato + asmi.
māgatosmi.example_2: Tenānusiṭṭho idha māgatosmi, vanibbako cakkhupathāni yācituṃ.
māgatosmi.translation_2: Instructed by him, I have come here, a mendicant, to ask for the path of the eyes.

tadate.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Probably a sandhi of tad (that) + te (to you), so "that (is) for you". The PEU suggests tadattha, but the context (yadicchase tvaṃ tadate samijjhatu) points to a sandhi. Doubtful; requires checking against the commentary.
tadate.example_2: Sa cakkhumā gaccha janassa pekkhato, yadicchase tvaṃ tadate samijjhatu.
tadate.translation_2: Go as one with vision in the view of the people, may that which you desire be accomplished for you.

parikkari.meaning_2: please do not; do not treat (us) thus
parikkari.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading (ka.) in the verse; the editors explain it as pari + ā + kari, a negated aorist of karoti with the prohibitive mā. The main reading is parākari, identical in meaning here.
parikkari.example_1: 58. Mā no deva adā cakkhuṃ, mā no sabbe parākari [parakkari (syā. ka. aṭṭha.), parikkari (ka.) pari + ā + kari = parākari];
parikkari.translation_1: Do not give the eye, O lord, do not do this to us;

sīviyo.meaning_2: Sivi; name of a people; one of the Sivis
sīviyo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text reads sīviyo, with the variant sivayo; nominative plural, referring to the Sivi people in the Jātaka verse.
sīviyo.example_1: 60. Yathā taṃ sivayo [sīviyo (syā.)] sabbe, sayoggā sarathā sadā;
sīviyo.translation_1: Just as all the Sivis, always with vehicles and chariots;

uddhatva.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant absolutive of uddharati; the commentary glosses it as uddharitvā. In the verse: having pulled out my eyes for the mendicant who desires them.
uddhatva.example_1: Uddharitvā [uddhatva (sī.), laddha tvaṃ (pī.)] cakkhūni mamaṃ jigīsato, hatthesu ṭhapehi [āvesi (sī.)] vanibbakassa.
uddhatva.translation_1: Having pulled out my eyes for the one who desires them, place them in the hands of the mendicant.

āvesi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 2nd singular of āvisati, used as an imperative in this verse. The PeU gloss āvesaka ("joined in") supports the same root. Some editions read āvesi as a short form of āvesehi.
āvesi.example_1: Uddharitvā [uddhatva (sī.), laddha tvaṃ (pī.)] cakkhūni mamaṃ jigīsato, hatthesu ṭhapehi [āvesi (sī.)] vanibbakassa.
āvesi.translation_1: Having pulled out my eyes for the one who desires them, place them in the hands of the mendicant.

uddhatvā.meaning_2: having pulled out; having plucked out; having drawn out; having extracted
uddhatvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive of uddharati (ud + √har, 'to lift up, draw out, pull out'). The text's variant uddharitvā confirms the reading; the form uddhatvā shows the contraction of -ari- to -a- before -tvā. Used here of pulling out the king's eyes.
uddhatvā.translation_1: Having pulled out the king's eyes, he offered them to the brahmin;

uparūḷhesu.meaning_2: healed; grown back; restored; (of eyes) recovered
uparūḷhesu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative plural in the text: 'when the eyes had healed'. From upa + √ruh 'grow up'; the pp rūḷha with the prefix upa giving the sense of recovery to a normal state.
uparūḷhesu.translation_2: Then, after a few days, when the eyes had healed;

nīdha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The form nīdha occurs in Jātaka verse, apparently as an indeclinable meaning 'here' or 'now'. Its analysis is uncertain; it may be a sandhi or a rare particle. The related PEU entry nīgha is different.

vidadhāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 3rd singular present of vidadhāti (vi + √dhā). In the verse it means 'produces (wealth)'. The PEU entry suggests 'arrange and reform'.
vidadhāti.example_2: 87. Na sippametaṃ vidadhāti bhogaṃ, na bandhuvā [na bandhavā (sī. syā. ka.)] na sarīravaṇṇo yo [na sarīrāvakāso (sī. syā. pī.)];
vidadhāti.translation_2: “This skill does not produce wealth, nor do relatives, nor one's bodily appearance;

gorimandaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading at Ja 6 verse; the accepted text has goravindaṃ (probably go + ravinda, 'cow-lotus', i.e. a cowherd? or 'chief of cows'). Accusative singular in the sentence.
gorimandaṃ.example_1: Passeḷamūgaṃ sukhamedhamānaṃ, sirī hi naṃ bhajate goravindaṃ [gorimandaṃ (sī. pī.)];
gorimandaṃ.translation_1: Look at the mute prospering in happiness; for wealth visits the cowherd.

samabhicaranti.meaning_2: surrounds; gathers around; approaches from all sides
samabhicaranti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of samabhisaranti (√sar) in the verse. Present 3rd plural in the text.
samabhicaranti.example_1: 89. Dumaṃ yathā sāduphalaṃ araññe, samantato samabhisaranti [samabhicaranti (sī. pī.)] pakkhī;
samabhicaranti.translation_1: “Just as birds flock from all sides to a tree in the forest that has sweet fruit;

sabbakālamasaṅkhyaṃ.meaning_2: at all times without number; at all times uncountable
sabbakālamasaṅkhyaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of sabbakālaṃ (adverb, 'at all times') and asaṅkhyaṃ (adjective qualifying najjo, 'numberless'). Sometimes analysed as a compound, but the separate words are commoner; the form as it stands may be retained as a sandhi entry.
sabbakālamasaṅkhyaṃ.example_2: 92. Yametamakkhā udadhiṃ mahantaṃ, savanti najjo sabbakālamasaṅkhyaṃ;
sabbakālamasaṅkhyaṃ.translation_2: “The rivers flow into this great ocean, which I describe, at all times, without number;

saṃvidheti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 3rd singular present of saṃvidheti (causative of saṃvidahati). The form vidhe- represents the causative stem. Some grammars derive it from √dhā with the causative suffix -e, giving saṃvidheti; others relate it to √dhā with a different strengthening. The meaning 'arranges' fits the context.
saṃvidheti.example_2: Yaṃ paṇḍito nipuṇaṃ saṃvidheti, sammohamāpajjati tattha bālo;
saṃvidheti.translation_2: Whatever the wise person arranges with skill, the fool falls into confusion there;

mākaṅkhi.meaning_2: do not doubt; do not hesitate; do not wish
mākaṅkhi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Prohibitive (mā + present 3rd singular); sandhi of mā + kaṅkhati. Also analysed as mā + kaṅkhī (2nd singular). The line 'gaccha tuvampi mākaṅkhi' means 'go, and you too do not hesitate'.
mākaṅkhi.example_2: Gaccha tuvampi mākaṅkhi, jīvissanti tayā saha.
mākaṅkhi.translation_2: Go thou with them, and linger not, for they shall live with thee.”

ṭhāpasa.meaning_2: established; placed; set up; laid down
ṭhāpasa.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Text variant in the Jātaka verse (syā. ka.) for the reading of the verb; likely aorist 2nd singular ṭhāpesi, a causative form of √ṭhā. The printed text has ṭhāpasa, perhaps an alternative 2nd singular aorist ending -asa, or a misreading. Uncertain.
ṭhāpasa.example_1: 158. Etaṃ me upamaṃ katvā, putte vijjāsu vācaya [ṭhāpasa (syā. ka.)];
ṭhāpasa.translation_1: “By using this similitude all wisdom’s truths explain,

lohituṇhīso.meaning_2: having a red turban; wearing a red headdress
lohituṇhīso.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Bahubbīhi compound describing a king. Nominative singular in the verse.
lohituṇhīso.translation_2: Shines with a red turban, shining like the sun during the day.

vijigucchase.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 2nd singular present of vijigucchati, a desiderative/causative formation from √gup 1. In the text it means 'do you despise (it)?'.
vijigucchase.example_2: Mātari mayhaṃ naggāya, kinnu tvaṃ vijigucchase.
vijigucchase.translation_2: Why do you despise the calling we live by, when my mother is naked?

tomarāni.meaning_2: spear; javelin; two-pronged spear (used against elephants)
tomarāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Neuter plural in the text (tomarāni ca) in a list of weapons; often masc. in commentaries.
tomarāni.translation_2: Take up the bows, the javelins and the spears;

visīlaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text, agreeing with the noun it qualifies. Negated adjective of sīla.
visīlaṃ.example_2: Sīlavantaṃ visīlaṃ vā, vasaṃ tasseva gacchati.
visīlaṃ.translation_2: Whether virtuous or without virtue—one comes under his sway.

nopaseveyya.meaning_2: should not associate (with); should not keep company (with)
nopaseveyya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] na + upaseveyya (optative of upasevati, √sev). Sandhi of na + u- as no-.
nopaseveyya.translation_2: The learned one should not associate with the bad, but should associate with the good;

bhallāṭiyo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name; variant reading bhallātiyo in some editions. Nominative singular in the verse.
bhallāṭiyo.example_1: 186. Bhallātiyo [bhallāṭiyo (sī. pī.)] nāma ahosi rājā, raṭṭhaṃ pahāya migavaṃ acāri so;
bhallāṭiyo.translation_1: There was a king named Bhallatiya, who, having abandoned his realm, practiced hunting.

sāḷūrasaṅghañca.meaning_2: pack of dogs; group of hounds
sāḷūrasaṅghañca.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text joined with -ca (sāḷūrasaṅghañca); accusative singular, object of nisedhayitvā. The DPD PEU guide gives sāḷūra as "dog" here, though it is normally a kind of dog or jackal.
sāḷūrasaṅghañca.example_2: 187. Sāḷūrasaṅghañca nisedhayitvā, dhanuṃ [dhanu (sī. syā. pī.)] kalāpañca so nikkhipitvā;
sāḷūrasaṅghañca.translation_2: Having quieted his pack of hounds, and having laid down his bow and quiver,

sītodiyā.meaning_2: having cool water; with cold water (name of a river)
sītodiyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant sītodiyā in the text (Sinhalese and PTS editions), for sītodakā; here a river name or epithet of rivers, ablative/genitive singular or nominative plural.
sītodiyā.example_1: 189. Mallaṃ giriṃ paṇḍarakaṃ tikūṭaṃ, sītodakā [sītodiyā (sī. pī.), sītodikā (?)] anuvicarāma najjo;
sītodiyā.translation_1: “We wander through the Malla, Paṇḍaraka, and Tikūṭa mountains, and the rivers with cool water.

sattaliyothikañca.meaning_2: name of a flower (possibly a kind of jasmine or water lily)
sattaliyothikañca.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text sattaliyothikañca is a sandhi compound of sattali + yothikaṃ + ca; the entry is for the first element sattali, a noun used in a list of flowers.
sattaliyothikañca.translation_2: “And I was gathering aṅkolaka, atimuttaka, and sattali flowers,

oceyya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive form in -eyya, probably metrically shortened for ocayitvā (ava + ci + tvā). The PEU analysis oceyya = ava + ci + tvā agrees in meaning; the ending is irregular. In these verses it describes plucking flowers to make a garland or a burden.

yatthajjamaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of yattha (where) and ajja (today, now); variant yatthajjimaṃ. Part of a clause meaning 'where we will spend the night'.
yatthajjamaṃ.example_1: Idañca no hehiti santharatthaṃ, yatthajjimaṃ [yatthajjamaṃ (sī. pī.)] viharissāma [viharissāmu (pī.)] rattiṃ.
yatthajjamaṃ.translation_1: this will be our bedding, where we will spend the night.”

viharissāmu.meaning_2: will stay; will dwell; will spend (the night)
viharissāmu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] First person plural future in the text (viharissāmu in some editions for viharissāma).
viharissāmu.example_1: Idañca no hehiti santharatthaṃ, yatthajjimaṃ [yatthajjamaṃ (sī. pī.)] viharissāma [viharissāmu (pī.)] rattiṃ.
viharissāmu.translation_1: this will be our bedding, where we will spend the night.”

akaluṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading akaluṃ (accusative singular) for agaḷuṃ in the verse; a fragrant wood paired with candanaṃ. The PEU entry akalusa (na + kalusa) is a different word.
akaluṃ.example_1: 200. Ahañca kho agaḷuṃ [aggalu (syā. ka.), akaluṃ (pī.)] candanañca, silāya piṃsāmi pamattarūpā;
akaluṃ.translation_1: “And I, being heedless, was pounding eaglewood and sandalwood on a stone,

āliṅgiyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text the reading is āliṅgiyā, probably a metrical lengthening of āliṅgiya before the caesura; used adverbially with aññamaññaṃ, 'having embraced each other'.
āliṅgiyā.example_2: Āliṅgiyā aññamaññaṃ mayaṃ ubho, sakimpi rodāma sakiṃ hasāma.
āliṅgiyā.translation_2: we both embraced each other, and at times we wept, at times we laughed.”

tīhūnakaṃ.meaning_2: short of three; minus three; less three
tīhūnakaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Adverbial use with a number: 'three less' (sattasatāni tīhūnakaṃ = 703). Instrumental tīhi with ūnakaṃ; sometimes written as a compound adjective.
tīhūnakaṃ.example_2: 204. Tīhūnakaṃ sattasatāni ludda, yamidha mayaṃ vippavasimha pubbe;
tīhūnakaṃ.translation_2: “Seven hundred years and three, huntsman, since we were previously parted,

nvejja.construction: na + u + ajja? or ko + nvejja?
nvejja.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Probably a sandhi of na/ko + u/eva + ajja; uncertain. The commentary glosses ko nvejja seti and ko ajja setu.
nvejja.example_1: Kassajja mātāpitaro rudantu, kvajja setu [ko nvejja seti (ka.), ko ajja setu (?)] nihato pathabyā.
nvejja.translation_1: For whom must mothers and fathers weep today? Who lies here on the ground, destroyed?”

pothayitosmi.meaning_2: is struck; is beaten; is crushed
pothayitosmi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading for heṭhayitosmi in the verse; a passive-causative-looking 1st person singular with the -itosmi ending. Treated here as a present form of pothayati, causative of √puth (crush, strike); the syntax is doubtful.
pothayitosmi.example_1: Ahiṃsako reṇumanuppavissa, puttena te heṭhayitosmi [pothayitosmi (ka.)] deva.
pothayitosmi.translation_1: I am a non-harmer, having entered the dust, yet I have been annoyed by your son, O King.”

āgañchu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text reading āgañchu is probably a variant or metrical form of the aorist 3rd plural āgañchuṃ (the commentary gives āgañchuṃ, the pada text gives āgañchu), from āgacchati. The headword here follows the related PEU entry āgañchi.
āgañchu.example_1: 217. Āgacchuṃ [āgañchuṃ (sī.), āgañchu (pī.)] dovārikā khaggabandhā, kāsāviyā hantu mamaṃ janinda;
āgañchu.translation_1: “The guards with swords have arrived; let the executioners kill me, O King;

pāricaratappamatto.meaning_2: unremitting in tending; diligent in attending (the fire)
pāricaratappamatto.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of pāricara (from pari + car) and appamatta; modifies the implied subject in the verse. Nominative singular.
pāricaratappamatto.example_2: 218. Sāyañca pāto udakaṃ sajāti, aggiṃ sadā pāricaratappamatto;
pāricaratappamatto.translation_2: “Morning and evening he draws water, he tends the fire always, unremittingly;

dunnikkayo.meaning_2: hard to remove; difficult to uproot
dunnikkayo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Describes a bamboo (veḷu) in Jātaka verse 222; nominative singular in the text.
dunnikkayo.example_2: 222. Daḷhasmi mūle visaṭe virūḷhe, dunnikkayo veḷu pasākhajāto;
dunnikkayo.translation_2: “The root is firm, wide-spread, and grown; the bamboo thicket is hard to remove;

kinnūdha.meaning_2: what now here?; how is it that?
kinnūdha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of kiṃ nu idha; used rhetorically in verse.
kinnūdha.example_2: 224. Kinnūdha deva tavamatthi bhogā, pubbevahaṃ [pubbe cahaṃ (ka.)] devaloke ramissaṃ;
kinnūdha.translation_2: “What possessions of yours are there here, O King? Previously I enjoyed the heaven of the gods;

vebhaṅgo.meaning_2: failure; spoiling; loss of potency (of medicine)
vebhaṅgo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is nominative singular: bhesajjassa + iva vebhaṅgo, 'like the spoiling of a medicine'. Sandhi of vi + bhaṅga; written with e and aspirate bh.
vebhaṅgo.translation_2: Like the failure of a medicine, its result is bad.”

pabbajjamevābhimanohamasmi.meaning_2: indeed I am inclined only to the going forth; I am only intent on renunciation
pabbajjamevābhimanohamasmi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of pabbajjaṃ (fem acc sg) + eva + abhimanohamasmi (abhi + manohamasmi, 'I am inclined towards'). The long ā is the result of eva + abhi. The whole phrase reads 'I am indeed inclined only towards the going forth'.
pabbajjamevābhimanohamasmi.translation_2: With difficulty I am freed from execution today; I am indeed inclined toward going forth.”

yamuggatejo.meaning_2: whose power is like death; whose fiery energy is like death (an epithet of a snake)
yamuggatejo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of yama (death) + gata (gone, like) + teja (power). Vocative singular in the verse; also found as yamuggatejo in the text with the nominative sandhi ending.
yamuggatejo.example_2: 243. Yamuggatejo uragoti cāhu, nāgoti naṃ āhu janā janinda;
yamuggatejo.translation_2: “Crawling serpent, fierce as flame! So they called him: one there came,

māgacchi.meaning_2: do not go; did not go; not approach
māgacchi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] For mā agacchi: mā (prohibitive particle) + agacchi (aorist 2nd/3rd singular of gacchati). In the verses it seems to mean 'came' or 'approached', so the negative mā may be questionable.
māgacchi.example_2: 244. Kathaṃ nvayaṃ balaviriyūpapanno, hatthatta [hatthattha (sī. syā. pī.)] māgacchi vanibbakassa;
māgacchi.translation_2: “How could such a starveling wight catch a creature full of might?

dubbissasametamāhu.meaning_2: indeed this is said of the hard-to-believe; truly it is called difficult to trust
dubbissasametamāhu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound-sandhi, tentatively dubbissa + samaṃ + etaṃ + āhu ('truly, this is said to be hard to trust'); dubbissa could also be dubbissā with metrical shortening. Sandhi is uncertain, so the division and pos are open to review.
dubbissasametamāhu.example_2: 254. Addhā hi dubbissasametamāhu, yaṃ mānuso vissase amānusamhi;
dubbissasametamāhu.translation_2: “Superhuman beings may hardly win belief, they say.

tvevahaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of tu (but) + eva (indeed) + ahaṃ (I). Always followed by na ... bhaṇeyyaṃ in these verses: 'but I would not indeed speak a lie'.
tvevahaṃ.example_2: Sabbā ca najjo paṭisotaṃ vajeyyuṃ, na tvevahaṃ rāja musā bhaṇeyyaṃ.
tvevahaṃ.translation_2: Flow upstream the running rivers, I, O King! could never lie.”

saṃvaṭṭeyaṃ.meaning_2: would contract; would dissolve; would roll together
saṃvaṭṭeyaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Optative 3rd singular; the text reads saṃvaṭṭeyaṃ by metrical variation, with sī./pī. adding the -ṃ. Refers to the contraction of the world at the end of the aeon.
saṃvaṭṭeyaṃ.example_1: 256. Nabhaṃ phaleyya udadhīpi susse, saṃvaṭṭaye [saṃvaṭṭeyaṃ (sī. pī.), saṃvaṭṭeyya (syā. ka.)] bhūtadharā vasundharā;
saṃvaṭṭeyaṃ.translation_1: “Split the sky, the sea run dry, bounteous mother earth awry

mubbahe.meaning_2: would break off; would tear out; would uproot
mubbahe.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading (Sinhalese, Syāmarī, Pīṭaka) for muppate (mubbhati, muṭṭhahe is another variant); optative 1st singular in the sentence, used of uprooting Mount Meru.
mubbahe.example_1: Siluccayo meru samūlamuppate [mubbahe (sī. syā. pī. ka. aṭṭha.), muṭṭhahe (ka.)], na tvevahaṃ rāja musā bhaṇeyyaṃ.
mubbahe.translation_1: Crumpling roll, uproot Mount Meru, yet, O King, I could not lie!”

anukampasī.meaning_2: have compassion (for); pity; feel sorry (for); care (for)
anukampasī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 2nd person singular present of anukampati, addressed to the king (janinda). The PEU entries anukampaka and anukampana are related derivatives.
anukampasī.example_2: 261. Anukampasī nāgakulaṃ janinda, mātā yathā suppiyaṃ ekaputtaṃ;
anukampasī.translation_2: “As a mother would have done to an only well-loved son,

naccayuṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text has naccayuṃ, a variant reading of naccisuṃ; both are 3rd plural aorist forms of naccati, meaning 'they danced'. The aorist stem is nacca-.
naccayuṃ.example_1: Dibbā tūriyā pavajjiṃsu, nāgakaññā ca naccisuṃ [naccayuṃ (sī. pī. ka.)].
naccayuṃ.translation_1: Celestial harps made melody, fair serpent-maidens danced.”

sopassaye.meaning_2: with a resting place; with a couch; together with a pillow; furnished with support
sopassaye.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Alternative reading sāpassaye in the text; here the word describes a golden seat with a bolster or resting support. Locative singular in the verse.
sopassaye.translation_1: Where the bevy of fair maidens tread the halls with thronging feet.”

nīrajā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Formed with the negative prefix nī- (= ni-) and raja (dust). In the text it is nominative singular feminine, agreeing with bhūmi ('ground').
nīrajā.example_2: Antepure bhūmiyaṃ santharantu, nikkaddamā hehiti nīrajā ca.
nīrajā.translation_2: Take and spread them in thy palace till nor earth nor dirt be seen.”

bhandhituṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Infinitive with -ituṃ suffix (sandhi -a + i > -i). The text gives bhandhituṃ as a variant reading for bandhituṃ, suggesting a spelling change. Bandhati is the present 3rd singular.
bhandhituṃ.example_1: Bandhi naṃ [bhandhituṃ (syā. ka.)] anupubbena, āraññamiva kuñjaraṃ.
bhandhituṃ.translation_1: she bound him progressively, like a tusker in the forest.

raṭṭhāto.meaning_2: from the realm; from the country; from the kingdom
raṭṭhāto.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Ablative singular in -ā (raṭṭhā), with the emphatic/euphonic -to variant raṭṭhāto in some manuscripts (also raṭṭhato). The text reads samhā raṭṭhā ca khattiyo, "and the aristocrat from the realm".
raṭṭhāto.example_1: 301. Tañca rājā vivāhesi [nivāhesi (syā.), vihāhesi (pī.)], samhā raṭṭhā ca [raṭṭhāto (sī. pī.), raṭṭhato (ka.)] khattiyo;
raṭṭhāto.translation_1: The king banished him and the aristocrat from the realm;

virājayi.meaning_2: abandons; gives up; frees oneself from
virājayi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3sg virājayi in the text (with -i for -esi); means 'abandoned, gave up' here, with kāmarāgaṃ as object.
virājayi.translation_2: Then he, having gone forth, abandoned sensual desire;

vāvīkareyya.meaning_2: should one reveal?; should one disclose?
vāvīkareyya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of vā (or) + vīkareyya, optative of vīkaroti (to reveal, disclose). The variant reading vāvikareyya shows the same sandhi without the lengthened ī. Occurs in the Jātaka verse on revealing secrets.
vāvīkareyya.example_2: Nindiyamatthaṃ pasaṃsiyaṃ vā, kassevāvikareyya [kassa vāvīkareyya (ka.)] guyhamatthaṃ.
vāvīkareyya.translation_2: Whether regarding a blameworthy matter or a praiseworthy one, to whom should one reveal a secret matter?

vāvikareyya.meaning_2: should reveal; should disclose; should make known
vāvikareyya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Written vāvikareyya, resolved as vā + vikareyya (optative 3rd singular of vikaroti, 'to make manifest'). Alternatively vā + api + kareyya, but the sense 'reveal a secret to a friend' favours vikareyya.
vāvikareyya.example_2: Nindiyamatthaṃ pasaṃsiyaṃ vā, sakhino vāvikareyya guyhamatthaṃ.
vāvikareyya.translation_2: Whether regarding a blameworthy matter or a praiseworthy one, one should reveal a secret matter to a friend.

nipphādā.meaning_2: non-accomplishment; non-completion; state of not being brought about
nipphādā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading in the Jātaka verse; other manuscripts have anipphannatā or anipphādāya. Here it is likely na + nipphādā (a negated abstract noun) taken as an independent feminine in the phrase ā nipphādā. Senses of ṇipphāda (Sanskrit niṣpāda) mean 'accomplishment', so the negated form means 'until non-accomplishment / non-completion'.
nipphādā.example_1: Anipphannatā [anipphādāya (sī. pī.), anipphannatāya (syā.), ā nipphādā (?)] saheyya dhīro, nipphannova [nipphannattho (sī. pī.), nipphannatthova (syā.)] yathāsukhaṃ bhaṇeyya.
nipphādā.translation_1: A wise person should endure until it is accomplished; once accomplished, they may speak as they please.

kāvindo.meaning_2: lord of desires; master of pleasure; (name of) Kāma
kāvindo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Found in the verse as kāvindo; the variant kāmindo is given in the edition. The form is probably a metathesis or scribal error for kāminda (kāma + inda); the PEU entry is uncertain. Nominative singular in the text, used as an epithet of Kāma.
kāvindo.example_1: 329. Ābādhoyaṃ asabbhirūpo, kāmindo [kāvindo (sī. pī.)] naradevena phuṭṭho;
kāvindo.translation_1: This affliction is unworthy of a noble person, the Lord of Desires (Kāma) touched by the king of men;

saṃhīro.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Vocative singular in the verse. Probably from saṃ + √har (carry away), i.e. 'carried away by' (cāmisena). PEU gives 'deceitful; easily deceived'.
saṃhīro.example_2: Yo cāmisena saṃhīro, hadayattheno ca yo naro.
saṃhīro.translation_2: Or to one who is swayed by material gain, or to a person who is a thief of hearts.

sambodhayati.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Third person singular present of the causative of sambujjhati, used here in the sense 'makes known, reveals'. The root is √budh (know, wake up).
sambodhayati.translation_2: The person who reveals a secret matter that was not understood;

tāvanto.meaning_2: so many; of that extent; as many
tāvanto.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominative singular masculine in the text, agreeing with ubbegā. Same formation as yāvant and etāvant.

paccanubhutva.meaning_2: having fully experienced; having enjoyed; having partaken of
paccanubhutva.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Alternative form paccanubhuyya (absolutive in -ya) is given in the text and is more common. The absolutive of paccanubhoti; variant spelling paccanubhotvā. Used with gandhe rase: having fully experienced smells and tastes.
paccanubhutva.example_1: Gandhe rase paccanubhuyya [paccanubhotva (syā.), paccanubhutva (pī.)] sabbaṃ, araññaṃ sādhu muni so pasattho.
paccanubhutva.translation_1: Having fully experienced all smells and tastes, the forest is good, the sage is praised.”

yime.meaning_2: these (parents) of yours; these for you
yime.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of tava (your) + ime (these). The text reads tavīme; the variant tava yime confirms the split. Nominative plural masculine.
yime.example_1: Jiṇṇā ca mātāpitaro tavīme [taveme (sī.), tava yime (syā. pī.)], passeyyuṃ taṃ vassasataṃ arogaṃ [arogyaṃ (syā. ka.)].
yime.translation_1: And these parents of yours are old; may they see you for a hundred years, free from disease.”

mokkhito.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Past participle used as a predicate in the verse; nominative singular referring to the speaker. The form is from the causative stem mokkha- (cf. moceti, mokkhati).
mokkhito.example_1: svāyaṃ gahīto na hi mokkhito me;
mokkhito.example_2: 346. Ayaṃ pure luddamakāsi kammaṃ, svāyaṃ gahīto na hi mokkhito me;
mokkhito.translation_2: “In the past I performed a cruel action, this result of that has been seized by me, and I am not released;

orundhiyā.meaning_2: having obstructed; having restrained; having blocked
orundhiyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -iya (cf. orundhitvā) from ava + √rudh, with the initial o- by the usual ava > o contraction. Used adverbially before parirakkhissāmi; the PEU suggests the meaning 'having restrained/enclosed'.
orundhiyā.example_2: Orundhiyā naṃ parirakkhissāmi, māyaṃ puna luddamakāsi kammaṃ.
orundhiyā.translation_2: Restraining this, I will protect myself, so that I do not perform such cruel action again.”

ketakapupphanettaṃ.meaning_2: with eyes like ketaka flowers; whose eyes resemble screw-pine blossoms
ketakapupphanettaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Bahubbīhi compound describing a maiden's eyes. Accusative singular in the verse; fem form ketakapupphanettā would agree with kumāriṃ.
ketakapupphanettaṃ.example_2: 349. Passāmi vohaṃ daharaṃ [daharī (syā. pī. ka.)] kumāriṃ, mattūpamaṃ ketakapupphanettaṃ;
ketakapupphanettaṃ.translation_2: “I see a young maiden, like one intoxicated, with eyes like the ketaka flower;

abhutva.meaning_2: not having enjoyed; without having partaken (of)
abhutva.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Written abhutva in the text, variant of abhutvā; metrically shortened. In the Jātaka verse it is construed with bhoge, 'without having enjoyed the coils'.
abhutva.example_1: Abhuttabhoge [abhutva bhoge (syā. ka. aṭṭha.), abhutva bhoge (pī.), bhoge atutvā (ka.)] paṭhame vayasmiṃ, ādāya maccu vajate kumāriṃ.
abhutva.translation_1: In the prime of youth, without having enjoyed its coils, Death carries away the maiden.”

atutvā.meaning_2: having not enjoyed; without having experienced
atutvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A variant reading (ka.) for abhuttabhoge / abhutva bhoge in the first line; the sense is 'not having enjoyed'. Probably a miswriting of abhutvā. Absolutive, so stem and pattern are left empty.
atutvā.example_1: Abhuttabhoge [abhutva bhoge (syā. ka. aṭṭha.), abhutva bhoge (pī.), bhoge atutvā (ka.)] paṭhame vayasmiṃ, ādāya maccu vajate kumāriṃ.
atutvā.translation_1: In the prime of youth, without having enjoyed its coils, Death carries away the maiden.”

māgatā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi resolution of hatthattam āgatā; nominative plural of a past participle in -a agreeing with te.
māgatā.example_1: Ye ca bhutvāna vamiṃsu, te me hatthatta [hatthattha (sī. syā. pī.)] māgatā.
māgatā.translation_1: And those who, having eaten, vomited, they have come to my hand.”
māgatā.example_2: 42. ‘‘ Kathaṃ panime vihaṅgā [vihagā (sī. pī.)], tava hatthattamāgatā [hatthattha ’ māgatā (sī. syā. pī.)];
māgatā.translation_2: 42. “How did these birds come into your hands;

ekaceyyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Metrical sandhi of ekacce (nom. pl. of ekacca, 'some') with iyyā; the sī. and pī. editions read ekacceyyā. The commentary may analyse it as ekacce + eyyā, but ekacce iyyā fits the sense. Variant reading in the verse.
ekaceyyā.example_1: 366. Hatthīhi assehi rathehi pattibhi, parivāritā muccare ekacceyyā [ekaceyyā (sī. pī.)];
ekaceyyā.translation_1: 366. Surrounded by horses, elephants, chariots, and infantry, some may be freed;

pitaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Alternate form of pitvā. The word in the text is a variant reading (syā.) where other editions have pitaṃ (hi taṃ). If read as pitaṃ, it would be pita (nt) meaning 'boiled/drink' or past participle of pivati. Here glossed as absolutive of pivati, 'having drunk', though the context is unclear.
pitaṃ.example_1: 370. Sarāni khīyanti saselakānanā, sabbaṃ hidaṃ [hi taṃ (sī. pī.), pitaṃ (syā.)] khīyati dīghamantaraṃ;
pitaṃ.translation_1: 370. Great lakes with their rocks and woods decay; all this decays over a long period;
pitaṃ.example_2: Sabbaṃ hidaṃ [hi taṃ (sī. pī.), pitaṃ (syā.)] bhañjare kālapariyāyaṃ, taṃ me matī hoti carāmi dhammaṃ.
pitaṃ.translation_2: All this is broken down by the passage of time; this I know, so I will practise the Dhamma.

nijjhapanaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is nominative/accusative singular, object of karonti: 'they make appeasement of them'. From nijjhapeti, causative of nijjhāyati, though the derivation is uncertain.

heṭṭhakā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the verse heṭṭhakā is nominative plural, listed with aparādhakā and dūsakā as people who wrong others; the sense is probably "low, base, despicable" rather than literally "lower". Could also be read as a variant of heṭṭhā.
heṭṭhakā.example_1: 377. Aparādhakā dūsakā heṭṭhakā ca, labhanti te rājino nijjhapetuṃ;
heṭṭhakā.translation_1: 377. Those who commit crimes, do wrong, or cause harm, can appease kings;

bhallātiya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name in a list of kings; no sandhi.
bhallātiya.example_2: Mātaṅga sambhūta sivi sirimanto, rohaṇa haṃsa sattigumbo bhallātiya;
